lede: From 21:01 to 01:42 KST five paper accounts of $500 each ran against CME futures, FX, LSE shares and ETFs, and NYSE/Nasdaq ETFs on live, partly delayed prices. Three of them traded; two never found a trade their rules allowed. Together they lost $17.32 of $2,500 (−0.69%). Transaction costs were $15.91 of that loss. Before costs, no account made or lost more than $1.44.
verdict: Net results. QG-TREND −$10.27 (−2.05%), LAZYOWEN-NAIVE −$7.05 (−1.41%), QG-CORE −$0.01, QG-TACTICAL and LAZYOWEN-CAL $0.00 because neither traded. For comparison, an equal-weight buy-and-hold basket of all 23 instruments lost $0.26, and $500 of SPY bought at the NYSE open made $0.37.

No predictive skill showed up anywhere. Before costs the three active accounts made −$1.44, +$0.49 and −$0.46. The 49-session replay and the 14-variant stress grid agree: gross P&L is zero for every rule set and variant (every |t| ≤ 1.1).

QUANTGEN's refusal machinery is the part that worked. The cost gate turned down 137 candidates; the best expected 60-minute move among them was 2.2 bp against a 10–100 bp round trip (the best of the night, 3.8 bp, was a USO short with no route to trade). In the replay the same model without the gate loses $3.87 a session.

QUANTGEN's only gate-passing rule does not survive the move to 5-minute bars. QG-TREND made 25 trades, won 2, and paid $8.82 in costs, $6.40 of it on nine LSE round trips. Tonight was worse than 84% of its replayed sessions.

LAZYOWEN's money management held; its edge rule did not. No stake exceeded 6%, there were never more than 5 positions, and the worst drawdown was −1.4%. Fed overconfident odds, the 8 pp entry and 5 pp exit rules churned 70 trades with an average hold of 20 minutes; 59 of the 70 exits were edge-decay exits.

Five hours cannot validate a model. QUANTGEN had no paper, mock or forward trading record before tonight (its order book held zero fills and its forward-record queue was empty). Read it as an end-to-end pipeline test with one clear finding: at this horizon and these costs, turnover decides the result.

good: 138 candidates cleared the 2 pp probability floor. The cost gate refused 137 of them (the largest expected 60-minute move among those was 2.2 bp against a round trip of at least 10 bp), and the last, a USO short, had no route to trade. In the replay, the same model with the gate removed loses $3.87 a session (t −22).

The inverse-volatility weights put 54% of the basket in 10y and 30y Treasury futures, and bonds rallied (ZB +0.43%, TLT +0.50% over the window). ZB made $0.31 and ZN $0.17, offsetting oil (−$0.33) and the Russell 2000 (−$0.22). Gross +$0.49 beat the equal-weight basket's −$0.26, but costs took all of it, and over 49 sessions this mode averages −$0.63.
Futures were the cheapest place to be wrong
QG-TREND's nine CME trades lost $0.54; its nine LSE trades lost $7.44. The replay says the same: −$0.50 a session on CME against −$2.53 on LSE and −$3.15 on NYSE ETFs.
Hard limits and pre-written exits worked as controls

All 12 controls passed on the full population, one with a documented exception (the pre-patch re-entry) and the kill switches on design only because nothing came near them: every entry had an exit plan, no LAZYOWEN stake exceeded 6%, QUANTGEN never exceeded 1.0× gross, no fill used a quote older than 25 minutes, and the books reconcile to the cent.
The review caught a real defect before it cost anything

Adversarial review found that one missing GBPUSD quote would have made an account's cash NaN for the rest of the night. It was patched and regression-tested at 21:17 KST, and positions resumed from saved state.
bad: Four round trips lost $3.03: $0.52 of market loss and $2.51 of costs. Shell fell 0.96% in the window while the trend vote crossed both hysteresis bands within single 5-minute bars, so the rule bought, sold and bought again. In the replay SHEL.L loses $0.62 a session with a 2% hit rate.

A $125.69 position, the account's largest equity holding, paid $1.26 in round-trip cost on a 35-minute hold. Each 50 bp leg was 2.3 times the fund's 1σ hourly move. Its two trades lost $2.93, and ISF.L lost on all 61 of its replayed trades.
USO fell 1.73% and WTI futures 1.25% in the window. QG-CORE's oil sleeve lost $0.33 with a worst point of −1.95% of notional, and QG-TREND's USO trade lost $0.68 on a 42%-volatility instrument.
LAZYOWEN-NAIVE entered at a mean claimed edge of 23.8 pp. Its 10 NYSE ETF trades lost $2.99, of which $2.97 was cost. Only 6 of 70 trades reached their 60-minute resolution.
The inverse-ETF short route is uneconomic intraday
The one short through RWM (inverse Russell 2000) lost $0.34, of which $0.30 was cost. At 50 bp per side a cash account cannot short ETFs for minutes.
cmpNote: LAZYOWEN is a Korean guide (lazyowen.com, published 2026-10-06) to a Grok bot that paper-trades Polymarket prediction markets from a $50 virtual balance. Polymarket is blocked in Korea and prices binary events, so its edge source cannot be ported; its money-management rules can. Two accounts ran those rules on tonight's markets: one fed QUANTGEN's calibrated probability, one fed an overconfident momentum probability that plays the part of Grok's self-rated fair odds.

impl: Put the cost gate in front of every rule family. QG-TACTICAL's test (expected move must beat round-trip cost) is the only component that took a losing rule to zero, by refusing every trade. Slower bars and smaller Kelly fractions also cut losses in the grid, but every such variant stayed negative. Apply it to C3 trend and to any LAZYOWEN-style rule before an order is allowed.

Route short-horizon risk to futures only. Replay losses per session for QG-TREND: CME −$0.50, FX −$1.43, LSE −$2.53, NYSE ETFs −$3.15. Hold ETF or LSE exposure for days, never minutes, while the KIS cost is 50 bp per side.

Keep C3 on daily bars, where it was validated. Slowing it intraday helps but does not fix it: 30-minute bars with 0.4 hysteresis cut the replay loss from −$7.60 to −$2.95 a session, and gross stays at zero.

Add a cooldown after an exit. Five- to thirty-five-minute Shell and FTSE round trips lost 1.1–1.3% of notional each, 1.0% of it in costs. Blocking re-entry on the same instrument for one full decision bar would have removed 3 of those 6 trades.

Stop pricing fills on delayed feeds. Yahoo's LSE quotes ran about 16 minutes late and CME about 10. QUANTGEN's KIS client already quotes overseas prices; use a broker feed like that for fills, or treat delayed venues as signal-only.

Require a calibration record before any probability can size a trade. With calibrated odds the 8 pp gate never fired (largest edge 6.3 pp); with uncalibrated odds it fired 193 times and lost. Make out-of-sample calibration (Brier, AUC, PIT) a gate input, the way QUANTGEN already gates its volatility fans on PIT and Christoffersen tests.

Run QUANTGEN's own gate on any intraday rule before it trades. That gate asks for at least 100 trades, survival at 2× costs, 504 in-sample sessions and five out-of-sample years, which means years of intraday history from KIS or a vendor; Yahoo serves only about a week of 1-minute bars.

Close the review's open items and version the run. Fit GARCH on completed sessions only, keep zero-return rows in calibration, fix the USD/JPY exposure formula, and put QUANTGEN and paper_live under git so the config and engine hashes map to commits.

Replace five-hour tests with a forward record. A daily paper record through QUANTGEN's forward-record module (R-25), which reviews itself on monthly to 12-month windows, would measure what the gate actually validates.
amend: Calibration before the start: the first intraday model's intercept was a 60-day drift (bonds had fallen), which QUANTGEN's own drift study rejects. Refit with the intercept fixed at zero; the refit was written at 21:01:01, 40 seconds before the live start.

Accounts set before the start: with a calibrated probability neither the cost gate nor the 8 pp rule would let anything trade, so QG-TREND (QUANTGEN's only gate-passing rule family), QG-CORE (no-timing basket) and LAZYOWEN-NAIVE (overconfident odds) were added. All parameters frozen in config.py, hash ffbdfc4d489bcaf2.
One pre-patch defect fired: LAZYOWEN-NAIVE closed its 30y T-Bond short on edge decay and reopened the same short in the same step (about $0.03 of extra cost). Left in the ledger as executed.

Restart after an adversarial code review (4 lenses, 2 skeptics per finding). Fixed: a missing quote could turn an account's cash into NaN; same-step re-entry; a cadence check that skipped decision cycles; an unchecked final flatten. config.py unchanged; positions resumed from state.json.
limits: A session has 59 five-minute marks and a few dozen trades. QUANTGEN's own gate needs at least 100 trades and five out-of-sample years. Tonight is a forward smoke test of the whole pipeline, not a validation of the model.
Yahoo's CME feed runs about 10 minutes late and its LSE feed about 16 minutes late. Every fill used the last observed 1-minute close plus QUANTGEN's per-side cost; no order touched a market.
Synthetic notional for futures and FX

A $500 account cannot hold a CME contract. Futures and FX positions are dollar exposures (CFD-style) capped by the 1.0× gross limit; ETF shorts go through 1x inverse ETFs because a cash account cannot short.
The 49-session replay uses 5-minute bars, today's GARCH volatility on past days, and Yahoo's 60-day limit. The intraday model is out of sample on only the last 9 of the 49 replayed sessions.
